questions.explanation: A month is shorter than a year, so two months is shorter than two years.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: A holiday lasts 14 days. One week has 7 days. Complete: the holiday lasts 2 _____. Use hours, weeks or years.
questions.explanation: Seven days and seven more days make fourteen days, or two weeks.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept week or weeks.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: The months go August, September, October. A birthday is in September. Which month comes just before it?
questions.explanation: August is immediately before September.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: A class has a 1-hour lesson, then a 1-hour game. There is no break. How much time do the two activities take altogether?
questions.explanation: One hour followed by another hour makes two hours.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: A child says, “A month is shorter than a week.” Which correction is right?

options.A: A month is longer than a week.
options.B: A week is longer than a year.
options.C: A month and a week are always equal.

questions.answer: A month is longer than a week.
questions.explanation: A month contains more days than one week.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: Plan tomorrow from morning to night. Put these events in order: go to bed, eat breakfast, eat lunch.
questions.answer: Eat breakfast, eat lunch, go to bed
questions.explanation: Breakfast comes in the morning, lunch later in the day, and bedtime at night.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept breakfast, lunch, bedtime in this order, working from tomorrow morning to night.
questions.correct_answer: Eat breakfast, eat lunch, go to bed

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: Which duration is longest?
questions.explanation: A year is longer than a week or an hour.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: The plan is: paint, let the paint dry, display the picture. What happens just after painting?
questions.explanation: Letting the paint dry is the next event in the given sequence.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: The days go Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. A visit is on Thursday. Which day is just before the visit?
questions.explanation: Wednesday is immediately before Thursday.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: A calendar lists October, November, December. Which month comes between October and December?
questions.explanation: November follows October and comes before December.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept November.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: A game lasts 1 hour. A trip lasts 1 week. Which lasts less time?
questions.explanation: An hour is a shorter duration than a week.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: A child measures the wait from one birthday to the next in hours. Which unit would describe this wait more simply?
questions.explanation: The wait from one birthday to the next is one year.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question:
Use this calendar row.
Monday: 15
Tuesday: 16
Wednesday: 17
Thursday: 18
Friday: 19
The trip is on Thursday. What is its date?
questions.explanation: The Thursday column shows the date 18.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: Put these durations in order from longest to shortest: 1 day, 1 year, 1 month.
questions.explanation: A year contains months, and a month contains days.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept year, month, day in this order.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: Today is Saturday. Tomorrow is Sunday. When is Sunday?
questions.explanation: Tomorrow means the next day.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: A puppet show lasts 2 hours. A music show lasts 1 hour. Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: Two hours is a longer duration than one hour.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: The months go December, then January in the new year. Which month comes after December?
questions.explanation: The month sequence starts again with January after December.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: A club meets for 1 hour before lunch and 2 hours after lunch. Do not count lunchtime. How many hours does the club meet?
questions.explanation: One hour and two hours make three hours of club time.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept 3 or three hours.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: A week has 7 days. A holiday lasts 7 days. A child calls this “one month”. Which name matches the duration?
questions.explanation: Seven days make one week.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: The months go February, March, April. The sports day is in April. The picnic is in February. Which happens first?

options.A: They happen in the same month.

questions.explanation: February comes before April.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: Which pair describes a shorter time followed by a longer time?
questions.explanation: One hour is shorter than one day. The other pairs go from longer to shorter.

questions.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
questions.question: Plan a usual school day with these events: go home after school, arrive at school, eat lunch at school. Write them in order.
questions.answer: Arrive at school, eat lunch at school, go home after school
questions.explanation: Arriving comes first, lunch is during school, and going home is after school.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept arrive, lunch, go home in this order.
questions.correct_answer: Arrive at school, eat lunch at school, go home after school

questions.question: Look at these shapes: A is a circle, B is a triangle and C is a rectangle. Which has three straight sides?
questions.explanation: A triangle has three straight sides and three corners.

questions.question: A plate has a round, flat base. Which shape would you draw around its base?
questions.explanation: The edge of a round plate makes a circle.

questions.question: A square and a rectangle each have four straight sides. What else do they both have?
questions.explanation: Both shapes have four corners, even when their side lengths differ.

questions.question: You have three straight sticks. Describe how to join them to make a triangle.
questions.answer: Join the sticks end to end in a closed shape with three corners.
questions.explanation: A triangle is closed and has three straight sides.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept words or a drawing showing three sticks joined into a closed triangle. Do not require the words end to end.
questions.correct_answer: Join the sticks end to end in a closed shape with three corners.

questions.question: Sort these shapes: circle, triangle, rectangle, oval. Which pair belongs in the group with only curved edges?
questions.explanation: Circles and ovals have curved edges and no corners.

questions.question: A book cover is a rectangle. Which shape card has the same shape as the cover?
questions.explanation: The rectangle card matches the rectangular book cover.
questions.question_type: connect an object and a shape

questions.question: Three sticks make the bottom and two sides of a shape. Its top is open. What must you do to make a closed four-sided shape?

options.C: Add a stick across the top

questions.answer: Add a stick across the top
questions.explanation: Closing the gap adds a fourth side and makes a closed shape.

questions.question: A group is labelled "four straight sides". Name two familiar shapes that belong in it.
questions.explanation: Squares and rectangles each have four straight sides.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept any two distinct familiar four-sided shapes, or matching drawings. A rotated square is not a second shape type.

questions.question: You turn a triangle card so that one corner points down. What shape is it now?
questions.explanation: Turning a shape does not change its three sides or three corners.

questions.question: A square paper tile is cut from one corner straight to the opposite corner. What two pieces does it make?
questions.explanation: Each piece has three straight sides, so each is a triangle.

questions.question: Two same-sized square tiles touch along one whole side in a straight row. What is the outside shape?
questions.explanation: The two squares together make a longer shape with four straight sides and four corners.

visual.caption: Two equal square tiles share one whole side.

questions.question: Draw one shape with a curved edge and one shape with only straight sides. Name your shapes.
questions.answer: For example: a circle and a triangle.
questions.explanation: A circle has a curved edge. A triangle has only straight sides.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept a curved familiar shape and a straight-sided familiar shape, accurately drawn and named.
questions.correct_answer: For example: a circle and a triangle.

questions.question: Which pair could you group together because their flat faces are circles?

options.A: A round coin and a round tin lid
options.B: A book cover and a round coin
options.C: A triangle sign and a tin lid

questions.answer: A round coin and a round tin lid
questions.explanation: A round coin and a round lid both have circular flat faces.

questions.question: A toy ball and a small cardboard box are on a mat. Which statement describes a difference?

options.A: The ball has a curved surface; the box has flat faces

questions.answer: The ball has a curved surface; the box has flat faces
questions.explanation: A ball is curved all around. An ordinary cardboard box has flat faces.

questions.question: A group is labelled "no corners". It contains a circle, an oval and a square. Which shape must move out?
questions.explanation: The square has four corners, so it does not fit the rule.

questions.question: You want to print a circle using paint. Name a familiar object with a flat circular part you could press on the paper.
questions.explanation: A flat circular part leaves a circle-shaped print.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept a round lid, round coin, circular base of a cup or similar appropriate object. A ball alone is not a flat circular face.

questions.question: A large triangle and a small triangle are in the same group. Why do both fit?

options.C: Both must be the same size

questions.explanation: Triangles can have different sizes and still have three straight sides.

questions.question: A house picture has a square wall and a roof made with three straight sides. Which shape is the roof?
questions.explanation: A closed shape with three straight sides is a triangle.

questions.question: Which material is most useful for making the curved edge of a circle on a table?

questions.question: A recorder uses C for both "cat" and "car". Suggest two different symbols or short labels so the answers can be told apart.
questions.answer: Use CAT for cat and CAR for car.
questions.explanation: Different labels make it clear which category each answer belongs to.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept any two distinct, clearly mapped labels, symbols or drawings.
questions.correct_answer: Use CAT for cat and CAR for car.

questions.question: A tally record shows four blocks choices as |||. What change is needed?
questions.explanation: Four answers need four tally marks. The current record has only three.

questions.question: A teacher writes each child's chosen sticker as a word in a list. Why is it helpful to record the answers as they are given?

options.A: So only the last answer is kept
options.B: So the teacher can change the choices
options.C: So answers are less likely to be forgotten

questions.answer: So answers are less likely to be forgotten
questions.explanation: Recording each answer straight away helps keep a complete record.

questions.question: You counted the types of shoes children wore today. Which question can your record help answer?

options.A: How many pets do they have?

questions.explanation: Sandals are a shoe category, so the shoe record can answer that question.
questions.question_type: connect data to an answerable question

questions.question: Plan a class survey about choosing a story or a song. Say what you will ask and how you will record each answer.
questions.answer: Ask each child, "Would you choose a story or a song?" Put one tally under the chosen activity.
questions.explanation: Use the same question for each child and record each answer once.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept a clear one-choice story/song question and a suitable recording method using words, objects, drawings, tallies or a digital form.
questions.correct_answer: Ask each child, "Would you choose a story or a song?" Put one tally under the chosen activity.

questions.explanation: Four dots represent the four star choices; two dots represent the two heart choices.

questions.question: A picture graph uses one leaf picture for each collected leaf. What does a row of three leaf pictures show?
questions.explanation: Each picture represents one leaf, so three pictures represent three leaves.

questions.explanation: Count the dots. Spacing them farther apart does not add votes.

questions.question: Five children chose painting. The painting row shows only four dots. Each dot should stand for one child. What change makes the row correct?
questions.explanation: Five children need five dots. One more dot completes the row.

questions.question:

questions.answer: More children walked than came by bus.
questions.explanation: The walk row has four answers and the bus row has two.

questions.correct_answer: More children walked than came by bus.

Swings: ● ●

questions.question: The class votes for a pet picture. The results are: rabbit 2, fish 4, bird 1. Make a labelled picture or dot display using one mark per vote.
questions.explanation: Each row needs the same number of marks as the recorded votes.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept labelled rows with exactly 2, 4 and 1 marks, using a consistent one-to-one unit.

questions.question: Three children choose dancing. Each dot represents one child. Which row correctly shows their choices?
questions.explanation: Three children need three dots in a one-to-one display.

questions.question:

Drawing: ● ● ● ●
Reading: ● ●

questions.explanation: Drawing has more votes, but the reading row shows that not everyone chose drawing.

questions.question: A display has two rows of dots, but no category names. Why should labels be added?

options.A: To show what each row is about
options.B: To turn one dot into two votes
options.C: To make every row have the same count

questions.answer: To show what each row is about
questions.explanation: Labels connect each count to the category it represents.

Banana: ●
Make another display of these votes using squares instead of dots. Label both rows.
questions.explanation: Changing the symbol does not change the votes when each new symbol still represents one vote.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept correctly labelled rows of four and one squares, retaining one square per vote.

Teddy: ● ●

options.A: More children chose story than song

questions.question: The teddy row has three dots. The ball row must show the same number of votes. Use one dot per vote. Write the ball row.
questions.explanation: The ball row needs three dots to show the same number as the teddy row.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept a labelled ball row containing exactly three one-to-one marks.

questions.question: The data says: train 4, bike 2. A graph shows Train: ● ● and Bike: ● ● ● ●. What is wrong?

options.A: Both rows have too many dots
options.C: The category labels are on the wrong rows

questions.answer: The category labels are on the wrong rows
questions.explanation: The four-dot row should be train, and the two-dot row should be bike.

questions.question: A display shows Dog: ● ● ● and Cat: ● ●. You put the cat row first and the dog row second. Each dot still represents one vote. What changes?
questions.explanation: Moving whole labelled rows does not change their counts.

questions.explanation: A one-to-one display uses three, two and one symbols for these categories.
questions.acceptance_note: Accept three labelled rows with counts 3, 2 and 1, using any consistent one-to-one symbol.

questions.question: Six children choose bubbles. Each picture should represent one child, but the bubbles row has seven pictures. What should change?
questions.explanation: Six children need six pictures. The seventh picture is extra.

mapping.assessable_focus: Represent, locate, compare and order numbers through 120.
mapping.ixl_skill: Use place value to compare numbers up to 120
mapping.observed_format: Choose the greater numeral using place-value models; compare hundreds, tens and ones.
mapping.cognitive_load_note: A short comparison with a visual model and one choice.
mapping.coverage_safeguard: Include 101–120, charts and number lines; Roman numerals are not needed.

mapping.assessable_focus: Partition one- and two-digit numbers in several ways.
mapping.ixl_skill: Ways to make a number - tens and ones
mapping.observed_format: Identify a quantity then complete a nonstandard tens-and-ones partition.
mapping.cognitive_load_note: Two connected place-value decisions with a regrouping model.
mapping.coverage_safeguard: Include one-digit partitions and nonstandard partitions, not only digit naming.

mapping.assessable_focus: Quantify collections through 120 using equal groups.
mapping.observed_format: Count objects organised into ten-grids and a partial group.
mapping.cognitive_load_note: Little reading; visual grouping supports a numerical total.
mapping.coverage_safeguard: Every item quantifies or organises an actual collection; include grouping decisions.

mapping.assessable_focus: Add and subtract within 20 using models and strategies.
mapping.observed_format: Select a number-line model that bridges through ten, then complete the addition.
mapping.cognitive_load_note: Choose a strategy and apply it; avoid long stories.
mapping.coverage_safeguard: Cover subtraction and several strategies as well as make-ten addition.

mapping.assessable_focus: Model additive situations, including simple money transactions.
mapping.ixl_skill: Word problems with change unknown - up to 10
mapping.observed_format: Use known start and finish amounts to find an unknown change; a cube model explains the missing part.
mapping.cognitive_load_note: Short practical context, one unknown, model-supported solution.
mapping.coverage_safeguard: Include Australian money, comparisons, missing parts and making representations.

mapping.observed_format: Read a total partitioned into equal groups and enter the size of one group.
mapping.cognitive_load_note: One concrete grouping decision supported by a diagram.
mapping.coverage_safeguard: Include both number of groups and size of each group; avoid formal division notation.

mapping.assessable_focus: Recognise, continue and create growing patterns by 2, 5 and 10.
mapping.observed_format: Complete a missing total in a small table of growing equal groups.
mapping.cognitive_load_note: Read a simple relation and extend one step.
mapping.coverage_safeguard: Include pictures, rules, repair and independent creation, not just next-number recall.

mapping.assessable_focus: Continue and create repeating patterns; identify the repeat unit.
mapping.observed_format: Construct a shape sequence from a repeat unit and continue it.
mapping.cognitive_load_note: Short construction task with a visible repeating unit.
mapping.coverage_safeguard: Keep repeating patterns separate from growing patterns; use several representations.

mapping.skill_title: Comparing Length, Mass, Capacity and Duration
mapping.assessable_focus: Compare and order four measurement attributes; give reasons.
mapping.observed_format: Compare two object lengths through the same intermediate reference.
mapping.cognitive_load_note: Read two visual comparisons and make one inference.
mapping.coverage_safeguard: Cover mass, capacity and duration as well as length; use supplied evidence.

mapping.assessable_focus: Measure length with equal informal units placed end-to-end.
mapping.observed_format: Place informal units against a line and enter the count; solution checks alignment, gaps and overlaps.
mapping.cognitive_load_note: Direct visual measurement with a brief numerical response.
mapping.coverage_safeguard: Include measuring and diagnosing placement, not only rules about measuring.

mapping.skill_title: Time: Years, Months, Weeks, Days and Hours
mapping.assessable_focus: Describe durations and event sequences using familiar time units.
mapping.observed_format: Locate a date in a calendar and choose its weekday from column headings.
mapping.cognitive_load_note: Read a small labelled display and make one selection.
mapping.coverage_safeguard: Add duration and sequence across all five units; avoid half-hour clock-reading scope drift.

mapping.assessable_focus: Make, compare and classify familiar shapes and environmental objects.
mapping.observed_format: Choose a shared feature of two pictured shapes; explanation checks each shape.
mapping.cognitive_load_note: One feature comparison with low reading demand.
mapping.coverage_safeguard: Include construction, classification and environmental connections; avoid advanced solid trivia.

mapping.assessable_focus: Give and follow directions to move within a space.
mapping.observed_format: Select a shape at a named row-and-column position on a small grid.
mapping.cognitive_load_note: A short spatial instruction supported by a grid.
mapping.coverage_safeguard: Expand static-location reference to actual movement; define page viewpoint.

mapping.assessable_focus: Acquire and record categorical data in varied forms.
mapping.observed_format: Count a pictured category and complete its row in a frequency table.
mapping.cognitive_load_note: Match category to its record with one counting decision.
mapping.coverage_safeguard: Include collecting, recording and correcting records, not just comparing totals.

mapping.assessable_focus: Make one-to-one data displays and compare frequencies.
mapping.observed_format: Compare two category frequencies in a one-to-one picture graph.
mapping.cognitive_load_note: Read a small display, count and compare.
mapping.coverage_safeguard: Include making displays and discussing evidence; every symbol represents one response.
